sources.title: Official Government Portal: Gabon eVisa service
sources.publisher: Official Government Portal of the Gabonese Republic
sources.officialityEvidence: The official government portal publishes this current eVisa notice, identifies the electronic service and links the DGDI eVisa portal while limiting the service to air entry at Libreville.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Ce dispositif s’adresse ... aux voyageurs désirant se rendre au Gabon par voie aérienne.

sources.title: Gabon e-Visa: live DGDI portal
sources.publisher: Direction Générale de la Documentation et de l’Immigration eVisa service
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Government Portal directly links evisa.dgdi.ga as the Gabon eVisa service. The live portal responds as Gabon e-Visa but currently exposes no public nationality selector or eligibility schedule.

sources.title: Foreign Ministry: countries exempt from visa register
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Gabon
sources.officialityEvidence: Gabon’s official Foreign Ministry page links a visa-exemption register, but the page identifies its publication date as 12 October 2011. It is retained only to record that it is not a current comprehensive schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Publié il y a 15 Année, le 12/10/2011

sources.title: CEMAC: Member States
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC’s official Commission website identifies the six current member States, allowing Gabon’s five foreign Member-State ordinary-passport codes to be mapped.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Cameroun, le Congo, le Gabon, la Guinée Équatoriale, la République de Centrafrique et le Tchad.

sources.title: CEMAC Commission President interview on free movement
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: The current official CEMAC Commission account states that visa-free free movement for Member-State citizens is effective.
sources.supportingExcerpt: L’effectivité de la libre circulation des citoyens des pays membres de la CEMAC, sans visa, est une réalité indéniable.

sources.title: Common Convention on free movement and right of establishment
sources.publisher: Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa
sources.officialityEvidence: CEMAC publishes the Common Convention in its official legal archive. Its free-movement provisions cover Union Member-State nationals travelling as tourists and specify document and three-month conditions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: La libre circulation de ces personnes comporte le droit de se déplacer et de séjourner ... pendant une durée de 3 mois

policies.title: Foreign CEMAC ordinary passports: Gabon visa-free short-visitor entry
policies.summary: Current CEMAC sources identify Gabon and five other Member States and state that Member-State citizens’ visa-free free movement is effective. The Convention describes the tourist free-movement stay and document conditions. This policy maps only the five foreign CEMAC ordinary-passport codes; it does not use a legacy Foreign Ministry register or the eVisa portal to infer other exemptions.
conditions: Applies only to citizens holding ordinary passports of the five other current CEMAC Member States: Cameroon, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, the Central African Republic and Chad.

For tourism, the published Convention describes up to three months and requires the community traveller to produce a valid or recently expired national identity card or passport and an international health booklet. The current Commission account confirms visa-free movement but does not independently restate the duration; verify the Convention’s continuing implementation before relying on that limit.

Entry remains subject to applicable border, health, public-order, security and individual-admissibility controls. It does not establish work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee or special-document treatment.
The current Gabon Government eVisa notice is limited to air entry at Libreville; it does not change this visa-free CEMAC policy.
